# Baxi ASHP Control: controller navigation reference

Built 2026-10-24 from *Baxi ASHP Control installation, user and service
manual* (7887625 v04), cite as "Baxi ASHP Control IM, p.N". This is the
lookup the assistant uses to give installers button-by-button steps on the
Baxi user interface (MK2.2) on the indoor control unit used with the
Assure HP55 outdoor unit.

**Keep it separate from Panasonic.** Different buttons, menus and access.
Never use a Panasonic step, menu name or key combination on a Baxi, or the
reverse.

**Buttons confirmed (Donal, 2026-10-24)** from the manual's Fig.11 on p.15
(image saved at `manuals/baxi/originals/baxi-ashp-control-fig11-p15-buttons.png`):
three controls under the display. The manual text file lost the button icons
inside sentences ("1. Press the  button."), but the figure, the carousel text
on p.17 ("Display the carousel by pressing the Main menu button", "Scroll
through the menu by turning the button") and Donal's confirmation that the
centre knob scrolls to the options on screen settle the steps below. Two
Clearing the error memory was confirmed by Donal from the p.134 page image
(saved in originals/): press and hold the [Dial]. The child lock override
was confirmed from the 12.1 page image (p.106, saved in originals/): briefly
press [Menu] and [Dial] together. All button steps are now covered.

---

## C1. Buttons and screens (Fig.11, p.15)

Layout under the display, left to right: **[Back]**, **[Dial]**, **[Menu]**.

| Answer name | Manual label (p.15) | Where / symbol | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Back]** | 1 Back button | Small round button, left; curved back arrow ↩ | Back to the previous screen |
| **[Menu]** | 2 Main menu button | Small round button, right; three lines in a circle ☰ | Opens the carousel (main menu) |
| **[Dial]** turn | 4 Selection/validation button | Large rotary knob, centre; dot in a circle ⊙ | Turn to scroll through items or change a value |
| **[Dial]** press | 4 Selection/validation button | Press the centre knob | Select / confirm |

Display backlight (Tab.5, p.15): **blue** = normal operation; **continuous
red** = warning or blockage; **flashing red** = lockout. Standby after 5 min
with no button pressed; press any button to wake it (p.15). Turning the dial
on the home screen steps through the zone screens (p.16).

Menu paths in the manual are written " > Installer > ..." with the leading
icon lost. They start from the carousel, so every path starts with **[Menu]**.

**Installer level (p.41):** [Menu], select **Installer**, enter code
**0012**. All installer functions open. It times out after 30 min with no
action. The unit does **not** need to be switched off first (that rule is
Panasonic only). The "Installer level activated" icon shows on screen (p.16).

## C2. Carousel menus (Tab.8, p.17)

Operating mode · Domestic Hot Water On/Off · Heating temperature · Water
temperature · Temporary heating temperature change · Hot water boost ·
System holiday mode · User settings · Test mode · **Installer** (code) ·
**Finder** (parameter search, installer) · **Signals overview** (measured
values, installer) · Energy overview · System settings · Version information.
Menus shown depend on the system configuration.

Installer menu branches used in the manual: Installation setup (Heat Pump,
Zone1, Zone3, Zone2, Domestic Hot Water, Mixed/circul. DHW, Outdoor
temperature, Solar systems), Signals, Counters, Error history,
Commissioning > Test mode, Advanced menu (Set configuration code, Auto
detect, Reset to factory settings).

## C5. Start and stop (p.122)

Start: switch on the outdoor unit and the indoor unit (auto vent about
3 min), then any backup boiler. Shut down: switch off heating/cooling,
outdoor unit power, indoor unit power, backup boiler. For long absences use
System holiday mode instead of switching off (frost protection and pump
anti-seize keep running). After a fault: off, wait 3 min, then indoor unit
on first, then outdoor unit (p.124, p.129).

# Panasonic wired remote controller: navigation reference

Built 2026-10-23 from the two Panasonic manuals on file. This is the lookup
the assistant uses to give installers button-by-button steps on the wired
remote controller (the panel on the unit or wall, not a phone app).

- **Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32** (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5). Source:
  *Panasonic Service Manual, Mini Monobloc R32 J-series* (cite as "J-series
  SM, p.N"). The text came from the PDF's text layer, and most button icons
  inside sentences were lost ("Press  for 5 sec."). The original PDF arrived
  on 2026-10-24 (`manuals/panasonic/originals/Panasonic-J-series-Mini-Monobloc-R32-Service-Manual.pdf`),
  and the hidden-menu key combinations and error-history clearing (A4) were
  read from its page images.
- **Part B: K-series split Hydromodule + Tank** (WH-ADC0309K3E5/K3E5AN/K6E5/
  K6E5AN, outdoor WH-UDZ03/05/07/09KE5). Source: *Panasonic Installation
  Manual, Hydromodule + Tank K-series* (cite as "K-series IM, p.N"). Button
  steps here were read from the original PDF page images (pp.21-34), so the
  icons are known.

**Keep the parts separate.** The two manuals show the same button layout, but
menu lists, item numbers and hidden-menu key combinations are documented
separately. Never use a Part B key combination or menu item for a J-series
unit, or the reverse. If something is only in one part, say it is not
covered for the other model.

---

## Button names used in answers

Both manuals label the controller buttons A to G (J-series SM p.74, K-series
IM p.21). Use these names in every answer:

| Answer name | Manual label | Symbol on the button | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Menu]** | B: Menu | ☰ (three lines) | Open/close the main menu |
| **[▲] [▼] [◄] [►]** | C: Triangle (Move) | arrow keys | Select or change an item |
| **[OK]** | G: OK | ↵ (return arrow) | Confirm |
| **[Back]** | E: Back | ↩ (curved arrow) | Back to previous item |
| **[Quick Menu]** | F: Quick Menu | ⠿ (grid of dots) | Open/close the quick menu |
| **[Operate]** | D: Operate | ⏻ (power symbol, with LED) | Start/stop operation |

Layout on the panel (K-series IM p.21): top row Back, ▲, Menu; middle row ◄,
OK, ►; bottom row Quick Menu, ▼, Operate. Every list screen shows "Select"
(arrows) and "[↵] Confirm" in its footer.

---

# Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32

## A1. First power-up (J-series SM p.22, p.75)

1. Initialising screen shows for about 10 s, then the normal screen.
2. Press any button: the Language screen opens. [▲]/[▼] to choose, [OK].
3. Clock format 24h or am/pm: [▲]/[▼], [OK].
4. Date & time: arrows to set year/month/day/hour/min, [OK].
5. Back at the start screen. Press [Menu], select Installer setup.

If this initial setting is not done, the controller will not go into the
menus (p.75).

## A2. Main menu tree (J-series SM pp.23-36, p.75)

[Menu] opens Main Menu. Items 1-4 are user menus, 5-7 installer.
J-series SM p.23: "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting."

- **Function setup**: Weekly timer, Holiday timer, Quiet timer, Room heater,
  Tank heater, Sterilization (p.23)
- **System check**: Energy monitor, System information, Error history,
  Compressor, Heater (p.24)
- **Personal setup**: Touch sound, LCD contrast, Backlight, Backlight
  intensity, Clock format, Date & Time, Language, Unlock password (4 digits,
  default 0000) (pp.24-25)
- **Service contact**: Contact 1 / Contact 2 (p.25)
- **Installer setup** (pp.26-36, flow chart pp.76-77)
  - **System setup**, in this order: Optional PCB connectivity, Zone &
    Sensor, Heater capacity, Anti freezing, Tank connection, DHW capacity,
    Buffer tank connection*, Tank heater (only if Tank connection = Yes),
    Base pan heater, Alternative outdoor sensor, Bivalent connection,
    External SW, Solar connection*, External error signal*, Demand
    control*, SG ready*, External compressor SW*, Circulation liquid,
    Heat-Cool SW*, Force heater, Force defrost, Defrost signal, Pump
    flowrate. (*Only shown when Optional PCB connectivity = Yes; optional
    PCB is CZ-NS4P, p.66.)
  - **Operation setup**: Heat, Cool (cooling unlocked only), Auto (cooling
    unlocked only), Tank (only if Tank connection = Yes)
  - **Service setup**: Pump maximum speed, Pump down, Dry concrete, Service
    contact

## A3. Step-by-step recipes (J-series)

General path into any installer item:
0. **Turn the heat pump OFF first:** press [Operate] (⏻) so the operation LED goes out. Installer setup can't be opened while the unit is running (J-series SM p.23: "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting"; confirmed on site by Donal, HMG Field Notes 2026-10-23). Remind the installer to switch it back on with [Operate] when finished.
1. [Menu] (top-right button)
2. [▼] to **Installer setup**, [OK]
3. [▲]/[▼] to System setup / Operation setup / Service setup, [OK]
4. [▲]/[▼] to the item, [OK]
5. [▲]/[▼] (or [◄]/[►] on multi-field screens) to change, [OK] to store
6. [Back] to step out, [Menu] to close

**Check it changed:** open the item again and read the value back. Where a
setting has a visible effect, it is listed below.

| Task | Path after "Installer setup" | Options / default | Check it changed | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| External room thermostat (or internal, room thermistor, water temp) | System setup → Zone & Sensor | Without optional PCB: Water temperature / Room thermostat (Internal or External) / Room thermistor. Default "Room and Water temp." | Main screen sensor-type icon changes (p.21 lists Water temperature, Compensation curve, Direct, Room thermostat External, Room thermostat Internal, Room thermistor icons) | pp.26, 78; wiring examples pp.64-65 |
| 2-zone / pool | System setup → Optional PCB connectivity = Yes, then Zone & Sensor → 1 or 2 zone | Pool only on zone 2 | Zone 1 / Zone 2 appear in Operation setup | pp.26, 78 |
| Backup heater capacity | System setup → Heater capacity | 3 / 6 / 9 kW depending on model | Re-open item | pp.26, 78 |

| **Custom menu** | **[Menu] + [▼] + [◄] for 10 s** | Cool mode (default without), Back-up heater use/not use (disables frost-protection heater, may cause H75), Reset energy monitor, Reset operation history, Smart DHW (start/stop time, ON temp) | p.34 |
| **Forgotten password** | **[Back] + [OK] + [►] for 5 s** (only shown when locked) | Unlock screen appears, press Confirm, password resets to 0000 | p.34 |

## B5. Gaps (K-series)

- Quick menu contents are not listed in the K-series manual.
- Function setup and Personal setup items are not described.
- Error history contents and error reset steps are not described, and there
  are no K-series fault codes on file.
- The manual says LCD screens are "for instructional purpose only, and may
  differ from the actual unit" (p.21).

steps.title: Pipework and wiring finished
steps.text: All water pipework and electrical cable connections are properly done before filling or test run (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Pipe duct sealed and dry
steps.text: The duct carrying the flow and return pipes between the outdoor and indoor unit is sealed and has no water in it. A wet duct makes the unit run constantly and trip on F12 (HMG Field Notes – F12 high pressure trips on site).

steps.title: Cylinder sensor in place
steps.text: If there is a DHW cylinder: the cylinder sensor is fully in the sensor pocket at the correct position, so it reads the real cylinder temperature. A misplaced sensor causes F12 trips (HMG Field Notes – F12 high pressure trips on site).

steps.title: Fill and purge the water circuit
steps.text: Remove the cover (2 screws). Turn the air purge valve plug anticlockwise one full turn. Set the pressure relief valve lever DOWN. Fill at more than 1 bar through the water inlet until water flows freely from the pressure relief valve drain hose (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Antifreeze decided
steps.text: The manual says antifreeze must be added to the water circuit to stop it freezing at low outdoor temperatures; recommended propylene glycol 40% (to -20 °C) (J-series SM p.63). HMG TO CONFIRM: does HMG fill with glycol, or use water with anti-freeze valves? Whatever goes in, set Circulation liquid to match in stage 3.

steps.title: Expansion vessel big enough
steps.text: Built-in vessel is 6 L at 1 bar pre-charge, good for up to 150 L of system water without antifreeze. Over 150 L, or with glycol, add a vessel. If the highest point is more than 7 m above the unit, set the pre-charge to (height in m × 10 + 30) kPa (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Water pressure
steps.text: With all power off, the unit's water pressure gauge must read no lower than 0.05 MPa (0.5 bar); top up if needed (J-series SM p.62). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG cold fill pressure.

steps.title: Pressure relief valve tested
steps.text: Turn the lever horizontal and listen for the clack of water draining, then push the lever back down. If water keeps draining, switch off and escalate (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Power on, pump running, no leaks
steps.text: Switch on the supply and check the water pump runs and there are no leaks at the pipe connections. Refit the cover (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: RCCB tested
steps.text: With power on, press TEST on the RCCB: the lever drops to 0. Touch nothing else inside. Set the lever back ON (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Language, clock and date set
steps.text: About 10 s after power-up, press any button: choose the language, clock format (24h) and date and time, [OK] after each. The controller won't open the menus until this is done (J-series SM p.22, p.75).

steps.title: Get into Installer setup
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ so the operation light goes out, then [Menu] (top right) › Installer setup › System setup. Installer setup is locked while the unit runs (J-series SM p.23; HMG Field Notes – Can't get into Installer setup).

steps.title: Optional PCB connectivity
steps.text: Yes only if the optional PCB (CZ-NS4P) is fitted, e.g. for 2 zones, solar or SG ready. Otherwise leave No (J-series SM p.26, p.66).

steps.title: Zone & Sensor
steps.text: Set it to what's wired: Water temperature, Room thermostat (Internal or External) or Room thermistor; 1 or 2 zones with the optional PCB (J-series SM p.26, p.78). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG's preferred control on a standard job.

steps.title: Heater capacity
steps.text: Set to the backup heater size: 3, 6 or 9 kW depending on model (J-series SM p.26, p.78). HMG TO CONFIRM: which setting HMG uses.

steps.title: Anti freezing
steps.text: Factory setting is Yes (J-series SM p.26). HMG TO CONFIRM: keep Yes.

steps.title: Tank connection and tank heater
steps.text: If a DHW cylinder is fitted: Tank connection = Yes, then Tank heater = Internal or External (factory Internal, ON time 0:20). To use the tank heater also set Function setup › Tank heater ON (J-series SM pp.26-27, p.79).

steps.title: Bivalent connection
steps.text: Only if a boiler is connected: Yes › Auto or SG ready › pattern (Alternative, Parallel, Advanced parallel). Otherwise leave No (J-series SM pp.27-29, p.80).

steps.title: Circulation liquid
steps.text: Water or Glycol, to match what's in the system (J-series SM p.30, p.82).

steps.title: Pump flowrate
steps.text: ΔT (factory) or Max. duty (J-series SM p.31, p.82). HMG TO CONFIRM: which mode HMG uses.

steps.title: Heating curve (HMG)
steps.text: Operation setup › Heat › Water temp. for heating ON › Compensation curve. HMG: steel radiators -3 °C outdoor → 45 °C flow, 15 °C → 35 °C. Underfloor -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C. The factory curve (-5 °C → 55 °C) is over the HMG maximum, so always change it. On 2 zones set Zone 1 and Zone 2 (HMG weather compensation guidance; J-series SM pp.31-32, p.83).

steps.title: Maximum flow (HMG)
steps.text: Never above 45 °C on radiators or 35 °C on underfloor. On the Panasonic the -3 °C curve point is the maximum: there is no separate maximum flow setting in the manual (HMG weather compensation guidance).

steps.title: Outdoor temp. for heating OFF
steps.text: Factory 24 °C, range 5-35 °C (J-series SM p.32, p.83). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG value.

steps.title: ΔT for heating ON
steps.text: Factory 5 °C, range 1-15 °C. Not shown if Pump flowrate is Max. duty (J-series SM p.32, p.83). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG value (HMG pipe sizing assumes a 5 °C ΔT).

steps.title: Heater ON/OFF
steps.text: Factory: outdoor temp for heater ON 0 °C, delay 30 min, heater ON at 4 °C below target and OFF at 2 °C below (J-series SM pp.32-33, p.83). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG values.

steps.title: Tank timings
steps.text: Floor operation time (factory 8:00), Tank heat up time (1:00), Tank re-heat temp (-8 °C) (J-series SM pp.34-35, p.84). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG values.

steps.title: Sterilization (legionella)
steps.text: Operation setup › Tank › Sterilization: factory 65 °C for 10 min. Set the day and time in Function setup › Sterilization (J-series SM pp.23, 34-35, p.84). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG temperature, hold time and day.

steps.title: Air purge
steps.text: Service setup › Pump maximum speed › [►] to Operation › [▲]/[▼] to Air Purge › [OK]. Run it until the flow reading is steady. [Operate] stops the pump (J-series SM p.35, pp.151-152).

steps.title: Flow rate checked
steps.text: Read Flow rate on the same screen. Must be at least 15 l/min with the main pump running; low flow can cause H75 during defrost (J-series SM p.63). Nominal flow: 5 kW 14.3, 7 kW 20, 9 kW 25.8 l/min (HMG sizing guidance; J-series SM p.12). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG pump Max. Duty setting.

steps.title: Service contact
steps.text: Service setup › Service contact › Contact 1 / Contact 2: name and phone number (J-series SM p.36). HMG TO CONFIRM: installer's own number, Heat Merchants Technical Support, or both.

steps.title: Screed drying
steps.text: Only on a new screed floor: Service setup › Dry concrete › Edit, set stages and temperatures (25-55 °C), then ON. Follow the screed maker's schedule (J-series SM p.36, pp.155-156).

steps.title: Start the unit
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ to switch back on and run heating (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Pressure while running
steps.text: Gauge reads between 0.05 and 0.3 MPa (0.5 to 3 bar) (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: No leaks
steps.text: Check every water connection for leaks during the test run (J-series SM p.53).

steps.title: Flow rate, all zones open
steps.text: With the heating running and every zone valve open, read the flow: [Menu] › System check › System information › Pump flowrate. It should be at least 15 l/min and close to the unit's nominal flow from stage 6 (J-series SM p.24, p.63; HMG commissioning check, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.title: Flow rate, all zones closed (bypass)
steps.text: Close every zone so all the flow goes through the bypass valve. Read the flow again in the same way, and adjust the bypass valve until it reaches the required flow rate (at least 15 l/min). HMG TO CONFIRM: the flow rate to set across the bypass (the 15 l/min minimum or the unit's nominal flow).

steps.title: No errors
steps.text: [Menu] › System check › Error history: nothing new. Clear old install errors: [OK], [◄] to Yes, [OK] (J-series SM p.24, p.163).

steps.title: Water filter cleaned
steps.text: After the test run, clean the water filter and refit it (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Explain it to the customer
steps.text: Show the customer how to use the controller and how to look after the unit (J-series SM p.4).

steps.title: Unit left running
steps.text: Unit ON at the controller, covers refitted, and Error history clear.

steps.title: Pipework and wiring finished
steps.text: All water and refrigerant pipework and electrical cable connections are properly done (K-series IM p.12).

steps.title: Tank unit and pipework checked
steps.text: Tank unit properly installed on a concrete floor, no gas leak at the flare nuts, flare nut connections insulated, water drainage properly done (K-series IM p.12 checklist).

steps.title: Refrigerant side
steps.text: Refrigerant pipework, leak test and evacuation by an F-Gas certified installer. R32 is mildly flammable (A2L). The outdoor unit manual isn't on file, so the app has no step-by-step for this.

steps.title: Fill the DHW tank first
steps.text: Drain tap CLOSED, all taps and showers OPEN, fill through the tank connector: water should flow from the taps after 20-40 min. Open the drain tap for 10 s to release air, then close it. Turn the safety relief valve knob anticlockwise and hold 10 s, then back (K-series IM p.9).

steps.title: Fill and purge the heating circuit
steps.text: Turn the air purge valve plug anticlockwise one full turn. Pressure relief valve lever DOWN. Fill at more than 1 bar until water flows freely from the pressure relief valve hose. Don't block the hose outlet (K-series IM p.9).

steps.title: Expansion vessel big enough
steps.text: Built-in vessel is 10 L at 1 bar, good for up to 200 L of system water (tank unit piping is about 5 L). Over 200 L, add a vessel. Keep the height difference of the water circuit within 10 m (K-series IM p.10).

steps.title: Pressure relief valve tested
steps.text: With power off, turn the lever horizontal and listen for the clack, then push it back down. If water keeps draining, switch off and escalate (K-series IM p.10).

steps.title: Antifreeze decided
steps.text: HMG TO CONFIRM: water or glycol on the K-series. The K-series manual on file doesn't give a glycol recommendation. Set Circulation liquid to match in stage 3.

steps.title: Power on, pump running, no leaks
steps.text: Switch on the tank unit and check the water pump runs and there are no leaks at the connections (K-series IM p.9).

steps.title: RCCB/ELCB tested
steps.text: With power on, test the RCCB/ELCB and set it back ON (K-series IM pp.10-11).

steps.title: Winter warm-up
steps.text: In winter, leave the unit powered on standby for at least 15 minutes before the test run, so the refrigerant warms up and no wrong error code shows (K-series IM p.12).

steps.title: Language, clock, date and front grille
steps.text: Press any button: language, clock format, date and time, [OK] after each. When asked "Is O/D front grille fixed?" select Yes. With two controllers, the first to confirm a language becomes the main one (K-series IM p.22).

steps.title: Water pressure on the controller
steps.text: [Menu] › System check › System information › [▼] to Water pressure. Not lower than 0.05 MPa (0.5 bar) (K-series IM p.10, p.34). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG cold fill pressure.

steps.title: Get into Installer setup
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ so the operation light goes out, then [Menu] (top right) › Installer setup › System setup (HMG Field Notes – Can't get into Installer setup).

steps.title: Optional PCB connectivity
steps.text: Yes only if the optional PCB (CZ-NS5P) is fitted. Otherwise leave No (K-series IM p.13, p.25).

steps.title: Zone & Sensor
steps.text: Set it to what's wired: Water temperature, Room thermostat (Internal or External) or Room thermistor (K-series IM pp.13-14, p.25). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG's preferred control on a standard job.

steps.title: Heater capacity
steps.text: Set to the backup heater size; options depend on model (K-series IM p.25). HMG TO CONFIRM: which setting HMG uses.

steps.title: Anti freezing
steps.text: Factory setting is Yes (K-series IM p.25). HMG TO CONFIRM: keep Yes.

steps.title: DHW capacity
steps.text: Variable (factory) or Standard (K-series IM p.25). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG setting.

steps.title: Bivalent connection
steps.text: Only if a boiler is connected: Yes › SG ready, Auto or Smart. Otherwise leave No (K-series IM pp.26-27).

steps.title: Circulation liquid
steps.text: Water or Glycol, to match what's in the system (K-series IM p.29).

steps.title: Pump flowrate
steps.text: ΔT (factory) or Max. duty (K-series IM p.30). HMG TO CONFIRM: which mode HMG uses.

steps.title: DHW defrost
steps.text: Yes (factory) uses the DHW tank for defrost (K-series IM p.30). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG setting.

steps.title: Heating control
steps.text: Comfort (factory) or Efficiency (K-series IM p.30). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG setting.

steps.title: Electrical anode
steps.text: Yes on K3E5AN/K6E5AN models, No on the others: check it matches the model on the rating label (K-series IM p.30).

steps.title: Two controllers
steps.text: Only if two remotes are fitted: Installer setup › Remote control setup › RC selection = Dual (K-series IM p.33).

steps.title: Heating curve (HMG)
steps.text: Operation setup › Heat › Water temp. for heating ON › Compensation curve. HMG: steel radiators -3 °C outdoor → 45 °C flow, 15 °C → 35 °C. Underfloor -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C. The factory curve (-5 °C → 55 °C) is over the HMG maximum, so always change it. On 2 zones set both (HMG weather compensation guidance; K-series IM p.31).

steps.title: Maximum flow (HMG)
steps.text: Never above 45 °C on radiators or 35 °C on underfloor. On the Panasonic the -3 °C curve point is the maximum: there is no separate maximum flow setting in the manual (HMG weather compensation guidance).

steps.title: Outdoor temp. for heating OFF
steps.text: Factory 24 °C, range 5-35 °C (K-series IM p.31). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG value.

steps.title: ΔT for heating ON
steps.text: Factory 5 °C, range 1-15 °C (K-series IM p.31). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG value (HMG pipe sizing assumes a 5 °C ΔT).

steps.title: Heater ON/OFF
steps.text: Factory: outdoor temp for heater ON 0 °C, delay 30 min, heater ON at 4 °C below target and OFF at 2 °C below (K-series IM p.31). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG values.

steps.title: Tank timings
steps.text: Floor operation time (factory 8 h), Tank heat up time (60 min), Tank re-heat temp (-8 °C) (K-series IM pp.32-33). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG values.

steps.title: Sterilization (legionella)
steps.text: Factory 65 °C for 10 min (K-series IM pp.32-33). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG temperature, hold time and day.

steps.title: Air purge
steps.text: Service setup › Pump maximum speed, [◄]/[►] to Operation, [▲]/[▼] to Air Purge, [OK]. Run it until the flow reading is steady (K-series IM p.33).

steps.title: Flow rate checked
steps.text: Read Flow rate on the same screen. Must be at least 15 l/min with the main pump running; low flow can cause H75 during defrost (K-series IM p.12). Rated flow: 3 kW 9.2, 5 kW 14.3, 7 kW 20.1, 9 kW 25.8 l/min (HMG sizing guidance; K-series IM p.8). HMG TO CONFIRM: HMG pump Max. Duty setting.

steps.title: Service contact
steps.text: Service setup › Service contact › Contact 1 / Contact 2: name and phone number (K-series IM p.33). HMG TO CONFIRM: installer's own number, Heat Merchants Technical Support, or both.

steps.title: Screed drying
steps.text: Only on a new screed floor: Service setup › Dry concrete › Edit (25-55 °C, 1-99 stages), then ON. Follow the screed maker's schedule (K-series IM p.33).

steps.title: Start the unit
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ to switch back on and run heating (K-series IM p.12).

steps.title: Pressure while running
steps.text: System check › System information › Water pressure reads 0.05-0.3 MPa (0.5-3 bar). If not, adjust the pump speed; if that doesn't fix it, escalate (K-series IM p.12, p.34).

steps.title: Heating normal, no leaks, no odd noise
steps.text: Heating works, no abnormal sound, no water leaks from the tank unit during the test run (K-series IM p.12 checklist).

steps.title: Safety relief valve
steps.text: The DHW safety relief valve knob has been turned to release air (K-series IM p.12 checklist).

steps.title: Flow rate, all zones open
steps.text: With the heating running and every zone valve open, read the flow: [Menu] › System check › System information › Pump flowrate. It should be at least 15 l/min and close to the unit's nominal flow from stage 6 (K-series IM p.12, p.34; HMG commissioning check, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.title: Flow rate, all zones closed (bypass)
steps.text: Close every zone so all the flow goes through the bypass valve. Read the flow again in the same way, and adjust the bypass valve until it reaches the required flow rate (at least 15 l/min). HMG TO CONFIRM: the flow rate to set across the bypass (the 15 l/min minimum or the unit's nominal flow).

steps.title: No errors
steps.text: [Menu] › System check › Error history: nothing new (K-series IM p.34).

steps.title: Filters cleaned
steps.text: After the test run, clean the magnetic water filter and the water filter and refit them (K-series IM p.12).

steps.title: Explain it to the customer
steps.text: Show the customer how to use the controller and how to look after the unit (K-series IM p.1).

steps.title: Unit left running
steps.text: Unit ON at the controller, covers refitted, and Error history clear.

fieldNoteList.title: Can't get into Installer setup on the controller
fieldNoteList.product: Panasonic J-series Mini Monobloc R32 (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5); also applies to the K-series split controller
fieldNoteList.cause: Installer settings are locked while the unit is in operation. The J-series manual says "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting" (Service Manual p.23). The K-series manual doesn't say this.
fieldNoteList.fix: Press the power button ([Operate] ⏻) on the controller to switch the heat pump OFF, so the operation LED goes out. Then press [Menu] (top-right button) and go to Installer setup. Switch the unit back on with [Operate] when finished.

fieldNoteList.title: F12 high pressure trips on site
fieldNoteList.cause:
Two known site causes, on top of the manual's list (J-series SM p.192):
  1. DHW cylinder sensor not in the correct position, so it isn't reading the actual cylinder temperature. The heat pump keeps running to satisfy it and cuts out on high pressure.
  2. The duct carrying the flow and return pipes from the outdoor unit to the indoor unit isn't sealed and has water in it. The unit works constantly, never gets the dwelling up to temperature, and trips on high pressure.
  These are not causes of "flow temperature not achieved": flow temperature is sensed in the unit after the condenser, so the DHW sensor position and a wet duct don't affect it (Donal).
fieldNoteList.fix:
1. Check the DHW sensor is fully in the cylinder sensor pocket at the correct position, so it reads the real cylinder temperature. Refit and secure it.
  2. Check the flow/return pipe duct between the outdoor and indoor unit. If there is water in it, clear the water and seal the duct properly.
